native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: PC1 of the forms-of-capital PCA peaks at the very beginning of the Younger Bronze Age: the 1100 BCE slice has the highest PC1 of the whole 4300-500 BCE series (4.51 sign-fixed units; PC1 = 30.3% of variance, oriented positively along Copper/Gold, Depot, Monument and other abundance indicators). The subsequent horizons 1000-500 BCE step sharply down (1000 BCE = 2.18, i.e., -2.33 PC1 units below 1100 BCE) and then drift to a low, roughly monotonic plateau (900 = 1.65, 800 = 1.92, 700 = 1.24, 600 = 0.81, 500 = 0.79), leaving 1100 BCE about 3.08 PC1 units (≈5.3 SD) above the 1000-500 mean of 1.43. The discontinuity reflects the loss of the terminal-OBA capital profile at 1000 BCE (Copper/Gold 2.85→-0.25, House Size 1.65→-0.32, Daggers 1.10→-0.48, Monument Count 1.35→-0.51) while Depots decay only slowly (3.38→1.73→-0.25→0.00). Group-level PCAs confirm this for symbolic (+2.24), social (+3.19) and economic (+1.83) capital, with cultural capital (pottery form/decoration) the sole exception (-0.40) because pottery-decoration diversity keeps rising in the YBA. Sensitivity checks (YBA-only PCA, exclusion of near-degenerate ZSichel, annual-interpolated century-bin means) preserve the sign of the contrast (+6.74, +3.06, +1.96 respectively), so the conclusion is robust to PCA scope, though its magnitude is not.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (39 rows x 12 Z variables, German decimal commas parsed, no missing values; century slices 4300-500 BCE; YBA = 7 rows 1100-500 BCE verified identical to the raw slice values in time_series_data.csv). Primary analysis: column-standardized correlation-matrix PCA (numpy eigh) on the full 39x12 matrix; PC1 sign fixed by positive mean loading on ZCU_AU/ZHort/Zamber/ZMonument; PC1 extracted per slice; 1100 BCE compared with each of 1000-900-800-700-600-500 BCE and their mean. Sensitivities: (a) YBA-only 7x12 PCA with zero-variance columns (ZSichel, ZKeform) dropped, (b) full-series PCA without ZSichel, (c) PCA on annual *_inter columns of time_series_data.csv averaged into century bins. Supplementary per-group PCAs (symbolic/social/cultural/economic per confirmed mapping). Outputs: analysis/pca_capital.py (executed), analysis/run_log.txt, analysis/pc1_by_slice_primary.csv, analysis/pc1_yba_sensitivity.csv.
